author: aobolensk
title: iGPU func tests fail en masse - no supported GPU devices found on runner
signature: Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed: [GPU] Can't get <PROPERTY> property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU Tests (func) / GPU
failed_jobs.symptom: clinfo reports 'Number of platforms 0' at job start; every GPU func test fails immediately at plugin construction before any test-specific logic runs

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check fails because the iGPU func test job failed

key_errors:
C++ exception with description "Exception from src/inference/src/cpp/core.cpp:272:
Exception from src/inference/src/dev/plugin.cpp:112:
Check '!m_device_map.empty()' failed at src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/plugin/plugin.cpp:593:
[GPU] Can't get DEVICE_TYPE property as no supported devices found or an error happened during devices query.
[GPU] Please check OpenVINO documentation for GPU drivers setup guide." thrown in the test body.
root_cause: The OpenCL runtime on the iGPU self-hosted runner reported 'Number of platforms 0' via `clinfo` before any test executed, meaning the Intel GPU driver/OpenCL ICD stack did not expose any compute devices to the container at job start (despite the container being created with `--device /dev/dri/renderD128:/dev/dri/renderD128`). Every GPU-dependent test in ov_gpu_func_tests therefore failed identically at OpenVINO GPU plugin construction time (the '!m_device_map.empty()' check in plugin.cpp:593), well before reaching any test-specific logic. The triggering commit (#38591) only touches RV64 Snippets Mod codegen for negative inputs and does not touch GPU plugin device enumeration or driver/runner setup, so this is not a code regression. This is the 4th recorded occurrence of the identical signature on this runner pool within the same day (previously at 09:11, 10:26, and 19:35 UTC), strongly indicating a persistent/recurring GPU driver or runner-provisioning problem on the iGPU self-hosted runner pool rather than a one-off blip.
reproduction_steps: Not reproducible from the commit diff; the failure is runner-environment-specific. To diagnose: SSH into the affected iGPU self-hosted runner, confirm `/dev/dri/renderD128` is present and accessible to the container's group IDs, then run `clinfo` inside the same container image (openvinogithubactions.azurecr.io/ov_test/ubuntu_22_04_x64_igpu) and check whether 'Number of platforms' is 0; if so, reinstall/reload the Intel GPU (NEO compute-runtime) OpenCL driver stack and compute-runtime kernel module on that host, then verify `clinfo` reports at least 1 platform before re-enabling the runner.
recommended_actions: Escalate to CI infrastructure owners: the iGPU self-hosted runner pool has now failed with identical 'Number of platforms 0' / zero GPU devices symptom 4 times in one day - likely a flaky/degraded runner host or driver crash loop.

Add a pre-flight health check step (e.g., `clinfo` assertion for platforms > 0) at the start of the iGPU func test job that fails fast with a clear 'runner GPU unavailable' message instead of letting 32927 tests fail individually.
Consider auto-cordoning/retiring an iGPU runner host after N consecutive 'no platforms' failures until manually re-provisioned.
Verify the Intel GPU driver/NEO compute-runtime version pinned in the ov_test/ubuntu_22_04_x64_igpu container image is compatible with the current host kernel/driver stack.
prevention_strategies: Add a runner health-check (clinfo/device enumeration) as a required pre-step for all iGPU jobs so driver/runner failures are caught and reported in seconds rather than after a 40+ minute full-suite run; monitor the iGPU runner pool for recurring zero-platform events and proactively replace/reprovision hosts that exhibit this pattern more than once.
historical_context: Identical signature recorded 3 prior times earlier the same day (runs 39387885502 at 09:11 UTC, 39398307308 at 10:26 UTC, and 39472332829 at 19:35 UTC), all on the same iGPU runner pool with the same 'Number of platforms 0' symptom and the same '!m_device_map.empty()' assertion. None were attributable to the respective triggering commits, consistent with an unresolved runner/driver infrastructure issue.
